description: The Scythian king Scilurus, who ruled in Crimea in the 2nd century BC, strengthened his kingdom by drawing heavily on the skills and infrastructure of the neighboring Greek cities of the northern Black Sea. Through trade, political alliances, and control over urban centers such as Neapolis Scythica, the Scythians gained greater access to Greek masonry, fortification methods, metalworking, coinage, pottery, and other specialized crafts. Rather than simply copying Greek culture, Scilurus’ kingdom blended these technologies with traditional Scythian practices, creating a more urbanized and economically organized state while preserving its steppe military and cultural identity.
